adventure.name: The Lair of the Minotaur
adventure.description: What respectable castle doesn't have a minotaur pit to throw meddlesome thieves into? And you might just be mistaken for one of those thieves. This is one of the earliest Eamon adventures, written by Donald Brown just after the original Beginner's Cave. It is a good example of the style of the first adventures, circa 1980.
adventure.author: Donald Brown
adventure.intro:
You had arranged to meet in the town of Dunderhaven with your friend, Larcenous Lil. When you arrived, you learned that Lil had come into town flat broke, and had tried to pick up some easy cash by burglarizing a nearby castle.

She hasn't been seen since.

Making your own subtle entrance into the castle, all seemed to be going well until suddenly the lights go on and you see yourself surrounded by bowmen and a fat, ugly man on a throne. He sneers at you and says, "Well, boys, another thief. I guess we'll send this scoundrel to meet the first."

With that, he pulls a lever, and the bottom drops out of the floor.

You slide down a long, narrow chute, with stony walls close on either side. You you land with a thud on the floor of a dark chamber.
adventure.full_description: What respectable castle doesn't have a minotaur pit to throw meddlesome thieves into? And you might just be mistaken for one of those thieves. This is one of the earliest Eamon adventures, written by Donald Brown just after the original Beginner's Cave. It is a good example of the style of the first adventures, circa 1980.

vehicle.board_text: You push off — the boat rocks, then steadies under you.
vehicle.leave_text: You drag the boat up onto the shore.
vehicle.blocked_text: The river is far too swift to swim. You need a boat.

death_rooms.16: Light ahead — a grate blocks the river. The current is faster than your arms. The boat splinters against the iron, and the water takes you.

say_triggers.text: As you say the word, there is a small eruption from the center of the stone and an emerald pops out of it.
say_triggers.already_text: The stone is silent. It has already given up its emerald — the mirror's word holds no more power here.

dig_sites.found_text: The shovel strikes something — a rotted pouch, heavy with gold coins!
dig_sites.nothing_text: You dig a while and find only wet sand.

cursed_items.text: As you touch the jewel, an electric shock runs up your arm. You hear a voice chuckling as it says, "I told you not to touch it."

guarded_items.text: The High Priest snaps, "Hey! Get your hands off my books!"

characters.name: Skeleton
characters.description: There is an animated skeleton here, who has for a weapon ten very sharp bony fingers.
characters.first_encounter_text: The coffin lid bursts open — a skeleton lunges out, ten sharp bony fingers reaching for your throat!
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)

characters.name: Killer Bunny
characters.description: You see swimming towards you a large rabbit with soft tan fur and a maniacal look in his pink eyes.
characters.first_encounter_text: On the bank sits a small, soft, white rabbit. It turns its head. Its eyes are wrong. Its teeth are very, very wrong.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: A small white rabbit with bottomless black eyes and a taste for blood. It cannot be reasoned with, exactly — but it can be respected from a distance.

acts.label: Stay very still
acts.success_text: You go absolutely still. The rabbit's nose twitches once, twice... and it loses interest in you entirely.

characters.yield_text: The rabbit sits back on its haunches and begins washing its face, as though you had never been worth the trouble.
characters.spare_text: You back away slowly. The rabbit watches you go with its terrible little eyes. You feel you have survived something significant.
characters.portrait_description: A small innocent-looking white rabbit with subtly wrong pitch-black eyes and a fleck of red at its mouth, sitting by a dark river bank

characters.name: Wandering Minstrel
characters.description: You see floating three feet off the ground a huge disembodied eye.  It has no limbs, but from somewhere it is humming a song:  A Wandering Minstrel Eye.
characters.first_encounter_text: You see floating three feet off the ground a huge disembodied eye.  It has no limbs, but from somewhere it is humming a song:  A Wandering Minstrel Eye.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: A wandering minstrel who took one wrong turn years ago and has been performing for skeletons and priests since. Starved for an audience that claps. Knows every corridor by song.
characters.portrait_description: A threadbare cheerful minstrel with a battered lute, patched bright clothes gone grey with cave dust, hopeful eyes

characters.name: Black Knight
characters.description: You see a knight carrying a sword and outfitted in black chain mail.  He does not look friendly!
characters.first_encounter_text: You see a knight carrying a sword and outfitted in black chain mail.  He does not look friendly!
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: The Black Knight — an armored duelist who guards the crossroads because a vow binds him there. Courteous, implacable, weary of killing trespassers who never observe the forms. Honors courtesy with courtesy.

acts.label: Salute
acts.success_text: You offer a formal salute. The visor inclines a precise inch. "At last," the knight says, "one who knows the forms."

characters.yield_text: The black blade lowers. "Well fought, and well spoken. The vow binds me here — but it says nothing of you passing."
characters.spare_text: The Black Knight steps aside from the crossroads and salutes you — this time, first.
characters.portrait_description: A knight in scarred black plate armor, closed visor, longsword held in a formal guard, standing in a torchlit stone crossroads

characters.name: Priest
characters.description: You see a man dressed in flowing religious garb.  He is wearing chain mail and is carrying a mace.
characters.first_encounter_text: You see a man dressed in flowing religious garb.  He is wearing chain mail and is carrying a mace.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: A priest of Kalimar keeping the chapel and its prisoner. A true believer, brittle about it — he knows holding a woman chained to an altar is not holiness, and hates being reminded.

acts.label: Shame
acts.success_text: "Does Kalimar smile on chains, priest?" His mouth works. The censer trembles in his hand.

characters.yield_text: The priest sinks onto the altar step, head in his hands. "Take her. It was never... take her."
characters.spare_text: You leave the priest kneeling at his own altar — praying, this time, like he means it.
characters.portrait_description: A gaunt priest in dark ceremonial robes with a bronze censer, hollow-eyed, guilt and zeal fighting in his face, chapel candlelight

characters.name: High Priest
characters.description: You see a man dressed in the robes of a high priest.  He wears chain mail and has a morning star in his hand.
characters.first_encounter_text: You see a man dressed in the robes of a high priest.  He wears chain mail and has a morning star in his hand.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: The High Priest of Kalimar — proud, learned, and possessive of his library. More scholar than fighter; his faith is mostly bibliography at this point.

acts.label: Kneel
acts.success_text: You bend a knee before the altar of Kalimar. The High Priest's scowl softens into surprised approval.

characters.yield_text: The High Priest lowers his morning star, breathing hard. "Enough. Kalimar preaches mercy — occasionally."
characters.spare_text: He straightens his robes with immense dignity, as though the whole affair had been a doctrinal debate he narrowly won.
characters.portrait_description: An imposing elderly high priest in ornate temple vestments holding a morning star, surrounded by candlelight and old books

characters.name: Blacksmith
characters.description: You see a huge, burly man wearing the apron and gloves of a blacksmith.  He carries a hammer in his right hand that has strange red stains on it.
characters.first_encounter_text: You see a huge, burly man wearing the apron and gloves of a blacksmith.  He carries a hammer in his right hand that has strange red stains on it.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: The lair's blacksmith — a broad, soot-black man who shoes the minotaur's gates and mends the temple's iron. Not evil, just employed. Immensely proud of his anvil.

acts.label: Admire his work
acts.success_text: You run a thumb along a hinge he forged and say so. The hammer lowers. "Aye... that one came out well," he admits.

characters.yield_text: The blacksmith sets his hammer on the anvil. "I'm paid to smith, not to die. We're square."
characters.spare_text: He nods once, spits in his palm, and offers you his enormous hand.
characters.portrait_description: A broad-shouldered soot-covered blacksmith with a leather apron and forge hammer, firelit smithy, gruff but honest face

characters.name: Gypsy
characters.description: You see a carefree Gypsy here, playing an accordion.  His music is so lovely that you almost fail to notice the wicked broad sword lying next to him.
characters.first_encounter_text: You see a carefree Gypsy here, playing an accordion.  His music is so lovely that you almost fail to notice the wicked broad sword lying next to him.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: A traveling fortune-teller camped in the clearing beyond the lair — sharp-eyed, unhurried, amused by adventurers. Knows more about the castle above than she says.

acts.label: Cross her palm
acts.success_text: You press a coin into her palm. She smiles like a door unlocking. "Now THAT is how a fortune begins."

characters.yield_text: She raises her hands, still smiling. "Peace, traveler. The cards never said we had to be enemies."
characters.spare_text: "Wise," she says, shuffling her worn cards. "The hanged man was never your card anyway."
characters.portrait_description: A weathered traveling fortune teller in layered shawls and coin jewelry beside a camp fire, knowing smile, worn tarot cards

characters.name: Larcenous Lil
characters.description: You see your old pal, Larcenous Lil! She thanks you for freeing her. She is rubbing her wrists from where the chains cut into her skin, but she otherwise seems unharmed.
characters.first_encounter_text: Chained by the altar is a woman you would know anywhere — Larcenous Lil, looking bored with captivity and delighted to see you. "Took you long enough," she says.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: Larcenous Lil — a quick-fingered thief and the player's old friend, held captive in the chapel by the Priest of Kalimar. Sharp-tongued, unrepentant about the botched castle job, secretly relieved to be found. Loyal to those who come back for her.
characters.portrait_description: A wiry, sharp-eyed young woman with cropped dark hair and a crooked grin, wearing burglar's leathers, wrists chained but posture defiant

characters.name: Minotaur
characters.description: You see before you a minotaur, straight out of the legends with his bulls head, human body, and a very nasty battle axe.  He does not smell very clean.
characters.first_encounter_text: The walls shake with a bellow. Out of the dark comes the Minotaur — taller than any man, bull-horned, eyes like coals, a battle axe in its fists. This is the master of the lair, and you are in it.
characters.text_source: The Lair of the Minotaur (Donald Brown, c. 1980)
characters.persona: The Minotaur of the pit — a huge bull-headed warrior bred in darkness to kill the castle's cast-offs. He has never been spoken to as anything but a monster. Beneath the bellowing is something old and tired that remembers being calf-young. Respects courage; despises pity.

acts.label: Salute
acts.success_text: You raise your weapon in salute, as to a worthy foe. The Minotaur stops. No one has ever done that.

acts.label: Listen
acts.success_text: You lower your guard a fraction and simply listen. The bellowing falters into something almost like words — almost like loneliness.

telegraph.name: horn charge
telegraph.warn_text: The Minotaur drops its head — those horns are aimed at your chest!

characters.yield_text: The great axe drags to the floor. The Minotaur stands heaving, watching you with its coal eyes — waiting to learn what you are.
characters.spare_text: You step back and lower your weapon. The Minotaur regards you for a long moment... then turns, and walks into the dark of its lair, unhurried. Behind it, the way stands open.
characters.portrait_description: A massive minotaur warrior with great curved horns, coal-red eyes, matted dark fur, gripping a huge battle axe, painterly and grounded, menacing but weary
